fund_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the financial statements package needed for a 409A valuation. My accounting system of record is {{vendor}}. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) confirmation that {{vendor}} is my accounting system, (2) the fiscal period(s) or date range the valuation firm needs (typically trailing 12 months plus most recent quarter/month-end), and (3) how I want the output delivered (e.g., exported files or a shared folder).

Using my configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}} and:
1. Pull the Profit & Loss (income statement) report for the requested period(s) using {{vendor}}'s profit-and-loss retrieval capability.
2. Pull the Balance Sheet report as of the relevant date(s) using {{vendor}}'s balance sheet retrieval capability.
3. If available through {{vendor}}'s API, also pull the general ledger and trial balance for the same period to support the valuation firm's review.
4. Verify the reports reconcile (balance sheet balances, P&L ties to retained earnings) and note any anomalies, missing periods, or categorization issues you find.
5. Compile everything into a clearly labeled package (P&L, Balance Sheet, and GL/Trial Balance if pulled), named by period and statement type, ready to hand to the 409A valuation provider.

Done looks like: a complete, internally consistent set of financial statements covering the requested period(s), exported or organized in the format I specified, with any data quality issues flagged.

Report back with: which periods/statements were successfully pulled, where the compiled package is located, any reconciliation issues or gaps you identified, and any statements or data you could not retrieve so I can source them manually.

fund_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me complete step fund_003:n2 of our 409A valuation process: gather a cap table snapshot. Please ask me for any of the following you don't already have: (1) which equity-management platform we use ({{vendor}}), (2) our issuer/company identifier in that platform, and (3) where our data room or prior 409A records are located for reconciliation.

Using my configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}} and pull our current cap table programmatically — stakeholders, share classes, securities (SAFEs, options, common/preferred), and vesting states. If {{vendor}} exposes a documented API, use it to retrieve the capitalization table and stakeholder list; otherwise use the platform's dashboard export to pull the data into an open format (CSV/Excel). Also check whether {{vendor}} stores fair market values from any prior 409A valuations and retrieve those for reference.

Once you have the export, reconcile it against our data room: confirm total shares outstanding, fully diluted shares, outstanding option grants with strike prices and vesting schedules, and any recent SAFEs or convertible notes match what's on file. Flag any discrepancies (missing certificates, unrecorded transactions, stale vesting data) clearly.

Done looks like: a clean, current cap table snapshot exported in an open format (CSV/Excel), a short reconciliation summary noting any mismatches found versus the data room, and — if available — a note on prior 409A fair market values for context.

Report back with: the export file(s) or a link/location where I can access them, a bullet-point summary of total shares/option pool/outstanding securities, and a list of any discrepancies or missing data that need my attention before this snapshot can be sent to the valuation provider. Do not attempt to commission the valuation itself or contact any third party — this step only prepares the cap table data.

fund_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a 409A valuation order in {{vendor}}, our equity management platform, ahead of an authorized officer's sign-off. Do not submit or authorize the engagement yourself — this requires a human officer's approval.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: our {{vendor}} account login context (I will use my own configured credentials), our company legal name, entity type, most recent funding round details (date, price per share, amount raised), and the desired valuation date or refresh schedule (e.g., quarterly, or triggered by next round).

Actions to take:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials.
2. Navigate to the 409A valuation ordering/intake section.
3. Confirm our live cap table data in {{vendor}} is current and complete (share classes, option pool, outstanding grants, recent transactions) — flag any gaps or stale entries you find rather than editing them yourself.
4. Fill in the 409A intake form fields: company details, valuation date, most recent financing terms, and any requested financial/operational inputs, using the information I've provided.
5. Select or confirm the refresh cadence if the platform supports scheduled updates.
6. Save the draft order in {{vendor}} without submitting or authorizing payment/engagement.

What done looks like: a fully filled-out, saved draft 409A order in {{vendor}} with the cap table data verified as current, ready for an authorized officer to review and submit.

Report back to me with: a summary of the fields you filled in, any cap table discrepancies or missing data you found, the draft's location/status in {{vendor}}, and a checklist confirming everything is ready. Then stop for human sign-off — an authorized officer must review and formally submit the engagement.

fund_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the 409A valuation questionnaire that our valuation provider (e.g., Carta or similar) requires before they can produce the valuation report. Your job is to draft and pre-populate as much of the questionnaire as possible using our existing company records, then stop for my review.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have access to: our cap table export, latest financial statements (balance sheet, P&L, cash flow), most recent board deck or investor updates, details of any recent funding rounds or convertible notes, headcount and org changes since the last valuation, and any material business developments (new product launches, major contracts, pivots, litigation, etc.). Also ask which valuation provider's questionnaire we're completing and get me the actual form or portal link if you can access it.

Using these inputs, draft answers for all objective/factual sections: company overview, capitalization structure, financial history and projections, comparable company or transaction data if requested, and prior valuation details. Clearly flag any question requiring subjective business judgment (e.g., risk factors, strategic outlook, likelihood of exit scenarios, discount rate assumptions) with a placeholder noting 'FOUNDER INPUT NEEDED.'

Compile everything into a single organized draft (document or filled-in form fields) so I can review, correct, and add my own judgment answers efficiently. Do not submit the questionnaire or communicate with the valuation provider on my behalf — this remains a human step, and after preparing the draft you must stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the completed draft questionnaire, a list of flagged judgment-based questions needing my input, and any data gaps you found in our records that I need to fill before submission.

fund_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me track a 409A valuation order that I've already commissioned through {{vendor}}, our equity-management platform. The independent valuation firm typically needs 2-3 weeks to complete their analysis, and that waiting period remains a human step — you cannot speed it up or operate any screen during this time.

What I need from you: set up a lightweight monitoring routine so I know the moment the report is ready, without me having to manually check every day.

First, ask me for any details you need: my {{vendor}} issuer/account identifier, the date I submitted the valuation request, and how I'd like to be notified (e.g., a daily or every-few-days check-in message from you).

Then, on the cadence we agree on, use my configured credentials to query {{vendor}}'s fair market values endpoint (retrieve fair market values from the completed 409A valuation) to check whether a completed valuation now exists for my issuer. If no valuation is returned yet, report back briefly that it's still pending and note how many days have elapsed since submission versus the expected 2-3 week window.

Done looks like: either (a) you detect a completed fair market value record and report the effective value, valuation date, and any expiration/refresh date back to me clearly, flagging that the report has arrived, or (b) if we've passed 3 weeks with nothing returned, you flag that the turnaround is overdue so I can follow up with the valuation firm directly — since chasing the vendor is also on me, not something you can do automatically.

Do not attempt to approve, accept, or sign anything related to the valuation report itself when it arrives — that remains a human step for me to review and sign off on. Just detect completion and summarize the results for me.

fund_003:n6.prompt:
You are helping me review a completed 409A valuation report before it is formally accepted by the company. Please do the preparatory work only — final acceptance must remain a human act.

First, ask me for: (1) the PDF/document of the 409A valuation report (from whichever independent valuation firm we used), (2) the date of the underlying valuation event and the intended 'as of' date, (3) our most recent cap table or option grant data, and (4) any prior 409A report for comparison, if one exists.

Once I provide these, please:
1. Summarize the report's key outputs: fair market value per common share, valuation methodology used, valuation date, and expiration/validity window (typically 12 months or until a material event).
2. Cross-check the FMV and share counts against our current cap table for consistency (e.g., matching share classes, total shares outstanding, recent grants).
3. Flag any material discrepancies, unusual assumptions, or changes versus the prior valuation (if supplied), such as large swings in FMV, methodology changes, or missing sections (e.g., no discount for lack of marketability explanation).
4. Draft a concise summary memo for the officer/board listing: the proposed FMV per share, valuation date, expiration date, and any flagged concerns, plus a suggested board resolution/consent language formally accepting the valuation for IRS safe-harbor purposes.
5. Prepare a checklist confirming: report received, cap table reconciled, no unresolved discrepancies, and memo/resolution ready for signature.

Do not accept, adopt, sign, or approve the valuation yourself, and do not instruct me to do so via automated action — this decision carries legal weight for IRS safe-harbor reliance and must be an officer's own authoritative act. When your review and drafts are complete, present the summary memo, checklist, and any flagged issues, and then stop for human sign-off.
